name: BitBay
rootCause: the UsdcDaiV4Vault _withdraw liquidity==0 branch pays the vault entire DAI and USDC balance to the caller with no share-weighted cap, and reposition() is permissionless once the tick is outside the narrow LP range, so the attacker deposits one wei for a single share, swaps the Uniswap v4 pool to push the tick onto tickUpper, calls reposition to recompute a position whose liquidity rounds to zero and leaves the pooled funds as raw balance, then redeems that one share to sweep the whole 14838 DAI pool. Lost: 14838.466608989135865711 DAI swept from the vault by a single 1-wei share on Polygon (reproduced to the wei against the on-chain Withdrawn amount), the attacker then unwound the drained DAI plus flash-loaned capital to a net ~14,813 USDC profit

descriptions.text: the UsdcDaiV4Vault _withdraw liquidity==0 branch pays the vault entire DAI and USDC balance to the caller with no share-weighted cap, and reposition() is permissionless once the tick is outside the narrow LP range, so the attacker deposits one wei for a single share, swaps the Uniswap v4 pool to push the tick onto tickUpper, calls reposition to recompute a position whose liquidity rounds to zero and leaves the pooled funds as raw balance, then redeems that one share to sweep the whole 14838 DAI pool. Lost: 14838.466608989135865711 DAI swept from the vault by a single 1-wei share on Polygon (reproduced to the wei against the on-chain Withdrawn amount), the attacker then unwound the drained DAI plus flash-loaned capital to a net ~14,813 USDC profit

BitBay’s Polygon DAI/USDC vault, UsdcDaiV4Vault, was exploited. The attacker first called reposition() to force the vault’s liquidity to zero, then redeemed only one minimal share. Because _withdraw() sends the contract’s entire token balance when liquidity == 0 instead of the user’s proportional share, about 14,838.47 DAI (roughly $14,000) was drained.
